units.zh: 梁書卷第二十四 列傳第十八
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 24, Biographies 18
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume Twenty-four, Biographies Eighteen

units.zh: 蕭景 弟昌 昂 昱
units.en: Xiao Jing; his younger brothers Chang, Ang, and Yu
units.literal: Xiao Jing; his younger brothers Chang, Ang, and Yu

units.zh: 蕭景字子昭，高祖從父弟也。
units.en: Xiao Jing, styled Zizhao, was Emperor Gaozu's cousin on his father's side.
units.literal: Xiao Jing, courtesy name Zizhao, was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

units.zh: 父崇之字茂敬，卽左光祿大夫道賜之子。
units.en: His father Chongzhi, styled Maojing, was the son of Daoci, who had held the post of Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.
units.literal: His father Chongzhi, courtesy name Maojing, was the son of the Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia Daoci.

units.zh: 道賜三子：長子尚之，字茂先；
units.en: Daoci had three sons: the eldest, Shangzhi, styled Maoxian;
units.literal: Daoci had three sons: the eldest was Shangzhi, courtesy name Maoxian;

units.zh: 次太祖文皇帝；
units.en: the second was the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Wen;
units.literal: the second was the founding Grandfather, the Literary Emperor;

units.zh: 次崇之。
units.en: and the third was Chongzhi.
units.literal: the third was Chongzhi.

units.zh: 初，左光祿居於鄉里，專行禮讓，爲衆所推。
units.en: Earlier, while living in his home district, Daoci had devoted himself to ritual propriety and modest deference and was widely respected.
units.literal: In the beginning, while serving as Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia he lived in his home district, devoted himself to ritual and deference, and was esteemed by the multitude.

units.zh: 仕歷宋太尉江夏王參軍，終于治書侍御史。
units.en: He served in office as an aide to the Prince of Jiangxia under the Song Grand Commandant and died as Attending Secretary in the Bureau of Documents.
units.literal: In office he served successively as aide to the Prince of Jiangxia under the Grand Commandant of Song, and ended as Attending Secretary in the Bureau of Documents.

units.zh: 齊末，追贈散騎常侍、左光祿大夫。
units.en: At the end of the Qi dynasty he was posthumously appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.
units.literal: At the end of Qi he was posthumously awarded Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia.

units.zh: 尚之敦厚有德器，爲司徒建安王中兵參軍，一府稱爲長者；
units.en: Shangzhi was steady and generous, possessed of real moral weight. As Central Army Aide on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an under the Minister of Works, the entire princely establishment called him "the elder";
units.literal: Shangzhi was solid and generous with moral capacity; he served as Central Army Aide to the Prince of Jian'an under the Minister of Works, and the whole administration called him "the elder";

units.zh: 琅邪王僧虔尤善之，每事多與議決。
units.en: Wang Sengqian of Langye held him in particular esteem and frequently consulted him before reaching decisions.
units.literal: Wang Sengqian of Langye especially favored him; on most affairs he deliberated and decided with him.

units.zh: 遷步兵校尉，卒官。
units.en: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers and died in that post.
units.literal: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers and died in office.

units.zh: 天監初，追諡文宣侯。
units.en: Early in the Tianjian era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Literary Manifestation.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was posthumously given the title Marquis of Literary Manifestation.

units.zh: 尚之子靈鈞，仕齊廣德令。
units.en: Shangzhi's son Lingjun served as magistrate of Guangde in the Qi period.
units.literal: Shangzhi's son Lingjun served as magistrate of Guangde under Qi.

units.zh: 高祖義師至，行會稽郡事，頃之卒。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu's righteous army marched east, he took charge of Kuaiji commandery affairs, but died soon afterward.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu's army of righteous campaign arrived, he acted in the affairs of Kuaiji commandery; shortly thereafter he died.

units.zh: 高祖卽位，追封東昌縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: After Gaozu ascended the throne, Lingjun was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang with a fief of one thousand households.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang, with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 子謇嗣。
units.en: His son Jian succeeded to the title.
units.literal: His son Jian succeeded.

units.zh: 崇之以幹能顯，爲政尚嚴厲，官至冠軍將軍、東陽太守。
units.en: Chongzhi rose to prominence through ability and resolve; his administration was notably stern, and he eventually reached the posts of Champion General and Administrator of Dongyang.
units.literal: Chongzhi became prominent for capability and energy; in government he valued severity, and rose to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Dongyang.

units.zh: 永明中，錢唐唐㝢之反，別衆破東陽，崇之遇害。
units.en: During Yongming, Tang Yu of Qiantang rebelled; a rebel detachment overran Dongyang, and Chongzhi was killed in the fighting.
units.literal: In the Yongming era, Tang Yu of Qiantang rebelled; a separate force defeated Dongyang, and Chongzhi was killed.

units.zh: 天監初，追諡忠簡侯。
units.en: Early in Tianjian he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Loyal Simplicity.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was posthumously titled Marquis of Loyal Simplicity.

units.zh: 景八歲隨父在郡，居喪以毀聞。
units.en: Jing was eight when he accompanied his father to his post; his mourning conduct became renowned for its wrenching austerity.
units.literal: Jing was eight when he followed his father to the commandery; for his mourning he was famed for self-inflicted ruin.

units.zh: 旣長好學，才辯能斷。
units.en: As he grew up he took to learning, showed talent in debate, and had a gift for decisive judgment.
units.literal: When grown he loved study, was talented in debate, and able to decide.

units.zh: 齊建武中，除晉安王國左常侍，遷永寧令，政爲百城最。
units.en: During Jianwu in Qi he was appointed Left Regular Attendant in the Jin'an princedom, then promoted to magistrate of Yongning, where his administration ranked first among all the counties.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Principality of Jin'an, then transferred to be magistrate of Yongning; his governance was the finest among a hundred cities.

units.zh: 永嘉太守范述曾居郡，號稱廉平，雅服景爲政，乃牓郡門曰：「諸縣有疑滯者，可就永寧令決。」
units.en: Fan Shuzeng, Administrator of Yongjia, had governed the commandery with a reputation for integrity and fairness. He admired Jing's administration and posted a notice at the commandery gate: "In any county where a case is doubtful or stalled, take it to the magistrate of Yongning for judgment."
units.literal: Yongjia Administrator Fan Shuzeng had governed the commandery, famed for integrity and fairness, and held Jing's governance in high regard; he posted at the commandery gate: "Wherever a county has doubtful or stalled cases, they may be taken to the magistrate of Yongning for decision."

units.zh: 頃之，以疾去官。
units.en: Before long he resigned his post because of illness.
units.literal: Before long he left office on account of illness.

units.zh: 永嘉人胡仲宣等千人詣闕，表請景爲郡，不許。
units.en: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others went to the capital and petitioned to have Jing appointed commandery administrator, but the request was denied.
units.literal: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others went to the capital and submitted a memorial asking that Jing be made administrator of the commandery; it was not granted.

units.zh: 還爲驃騎行參軍。
units.en: He returned to the capital as Traveling Aide on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.
units.literal: He returned to serve as Traveling Aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.

units.zh: 永元二年，以長沙宣武王懿勳，除步兵校尉。
units.en: In the second year of Yongyuan, in recognition of the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Xiao Yi, he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, on account of the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

units.zh: 是冬，宣武王遇害，景亦逃難。
units.en: That winter Prince Xuanwu was murdered, and Jing fled into hiding as well.
units.literal: That winter Prince Xuanwu was killed, and Jing also fled into hiding.

units.zh: 高祖義師至，以景爲寧朔將軍、行南兗州軍事。
units.en: When Gaozu's righteous army arrived, Jing was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and put in charge of Southern Yanzhou affairs.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu's righteous army arrived, Jing was made General Who Pacifies the North and Acting Commander of Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 時天下未定，江北傖楚各據塢壁。
units.en: The realm was still unsettled; north of the Yangzi, northern settlers and Chu clans each held their own fortified stockades.
units.literal: At the time the realm was not yet settled; north of the Yangzi the northern migrants and Chu people each held fortified stockades.

units.zh: 景示以威信，渠帥相率面縛請罪，旬日境內皆平。
units.en: Jing won them over with authority and good faith; one chieftain after another came forward bound to beg pardon, and within ten days the entire region was pacified.
units.literal: Jing displayed authority and trust; chieftains came in succession with bound faces to beg forgiveness, and within ten days the whole territory was pacified.

units.zh: 中興二年，遷督南兗州諸軍事、輔國將軍、監南兗州。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongxing he was promoted to Supervisor of Military Affairs for Southern Yanzhou, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was transferred to Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Southern Yanzhou, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，封吳平縣侯，食邑一千戶，仍爲使持節、都督南北兗青冀四州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping with a fief of one thousand households and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief over North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, Champion General, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping county, with a fief of one thousand households, and continued as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the four provinces of North and South Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 詔景母毛氏爲國太夫人，禮如王國太妃，假金章紫綬。
units.en: An edict made Jing's mother, Lady Mao, Grand Lady of the State, with ceremonial standing equal to a princely grand consort, and granted her the golden seal and purple sash.
units.literal: An edict made Jing's mother Lady Mao Grand Lady of the State, with ceremony like a princely Grand Consort, and granted her the golden seal and purple sash.

units.zh: 景居州，清恪有威裁，明解吏職，文案無壅，下不敢欺，吏人畏敬如神。
units.en: As governor, Jing was pure, scrupulous, and commanding; he understood official duties thoroughly, kept paperwork moving without backlog, and left no room for deception below him. Officials and commoners alike revered him almost as a god.
units.literal: Jing governed the province with purity, scrupulousness, authority, and judgment; he understood clearly the duties of officials; documents were never blocked; subordinates did not dare deceive; officials and people revered him as a spirit.

units.zh: 會年荒，計口賑卹，爲饘粥於路以賦之，死者給棺具，人甚賴焉。
units.en: When famine struck, he counted households to distribute relief, set up gruel kitchens along the roads, and supplied coffins for the dead. The people depended on him heavily.
units.literal: It happened to be a year of famine; he counted mouths to give relief, set out gruel on the roads to distribute, provided coffins for the dead, and people relied on him greatly.

units.zh: 天監四年，王師北伐，景帥衆出淮陽，進屠宿預。
units.en: In the fourth year of Tianjian, when the imperial army marched north, Jing led his forces from Huaiyang and advanced to storm Suyu.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian the imperial army marched north; Jing led troops out from Huaiyang and advanced to slaughter Suyu.

units.zh: 丁母憂，詔起攝職。
units.en: When his mother died he entered mourning, but an edict recalled him to resume his duties provisionally.
units.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; an edict ordered him recalled to assume duties in a provisional capacity.

units.zh: 五年，班師，除太子右衛率，遷輔國將軍、衛尉卿。
units.en: In the fifth year, after the army withdrew, he was appointed Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then promoted to General Who Assists the State and Commandant of the Guard.
units.literal: In the fifth year the army returned; he was appointed Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then transferred to General Who Assists the State and Commandant of the Guard.

units.zh: 七年，遷左驍騎將軍，兼領軍將軍。
units.en: In the seventh year he was promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry and concurrently served as General of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry and concurrently served as General of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 領軍管天下兵要，監局官僚，舊多驕侈，景在職峻切，官曹肅然。
units.en: The Palace Guard controlled the empire's key military posts, and the supervisory offices had long been riddled with arrogance and extravagance. Jing's tenure was stern and exacting, and the bureaucracy quickly fell into order.
units.literal: The Palace Guard controlled the vital points of the realm's armies; the supervisory bureaus and officials had long been mostly arrogant and extravagant; Jing in office was stern and exacting, and the offices became solemn.

units.zh: 制局監皆近幸，頗不堪命，以是不得久留中。
units.en: The supervisors of the control bureaus were all imperial favorites and could scarcely endure his discipline, which is why he could not remain long at court.
units.literal: The supervisors of the control bureaus were all close favorites and could hardly bear his commands; for this reason he could not long remain at court.

units.zh: 尋出爲使持節、督雍梁南北秦郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、信武將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: Before long he was posted out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingling in Jing, and Suixian in Si, General of Trustworthy Martiality, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.
units.literal: Soon he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Suixian, General of Trustworthy Martiality, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.

units.zh: 八年三月，魏荊州刺史元志率衆七萬寇潺溝，驅迫羣蠻，羣蠻悉渡漢水來降。
units.en: In the third month of the eighth year, Yuan Zhi, Governor of Jingzhou for Wei, led seventy thousand men against Chan'gou, driving the tribal peoples before him until they all crossed the Han to surrender.
units.literal: In the third month of the eighth year, Wei Governor of Jingzhou Yuan Zhi led seventy thousand men to raid Chan'gou, driving and pressing the various barbarians; the various barbarians all crossed the Han to come and surrender.

units.zh: 議者以蠻累爲邊患，可因此除之。
units.en: Some at court argued that the tribes had long been a frontier menace and should be wiped out while they had the chance.
units.literal: Those in council held that the barbarians had long been a frontier trouble and could be eliminated on this occasion.

units.zh: 景曰：「窮來歸我，誅之不祥。
units.en: Jing said, "They have come to us in desperation. To slaughter them would be inauspicious.
units.literal: Jing said: "Having come to the end of their strength to submit to us, to execute them would be inauspicious.

units.zh: 且魏人來侵，每爲矛盾，若悉誅蠻，則魏軍無礙，非長策也。」
units.en: Besides, whenever the Wei invade they exploit our internal divisions. If we kill all the tribes, the Wei army will meet no resistance at all. That is no lasting strategy."
units.literal: Moreover when Wei people come to invade they always use contradictions; if all the barbarians were killed, then the Wei army would meet no obstruction—this is not a long-term plan."

units.zh: 乃開樊城受降。
units.en: He then opened Fancheng to receive their surrender.
units.literal: Thereupon he opened Fancheng to receive their surrender.

units.zh: 因命司馬硃思遠、寧蠻長史曹義宗、中兵參軍孟惠俊擊志於潺溝，大破之，生擒志長史杜景。
units.en: He then ordered Chief Administrator Zhu Siyuan, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the Barbarians Cao Yizong, and Central Army Aide Meng Huijun to attack Zhi at Chan'gou. They won a great victory and took Zhi's chief clerk Du Jing alive.
units.literal: He then ordered Chief Administrator Zhu Siyuan, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the Barbarians Cao Yizong, and Central Army Aide Meng Huijun to strike Zhi at Chan'gou and routed him greatly, taking alive Zhi's Chief Clerk Du Jing.

units.zh: 斬首萬餘級，流屍蓋漢水，景遣中兵參軍崔繢率軍士收而瘞焉。
units.en: More than ten thousand heads were taken; corpses floating on the Han covered the river. Jing sent Central Army Aide Cui Hui with soldiers to gather and bury them.
units.literal: More than ten thousand heads were cut off; floating corpses covered the Han; Jing sent Central Army Aide Cui Hui to lead soldiers to gather and bury them.

units.zh: 景初到州，省除參迎羽儀器服，不得煩擾吏人。
units.en: When Jing first arrived in Yong he abolished the welcoming retinues, ceremonial regalia, and display equipment and would not burden officials or commoners.
units.literal: When Jing first arrived at the province he abolished the welcoming retinue, ceremonial regalia, and equipment, and would not trouble officials and people.

units.zh: 修營城壘，申警邊備，理辭訟，勸農桑。
units.en: He repaired the walls and fortifications, tightened frontier defenses, heard lawsuits, and encouraged farming and sericulture.
units.literal: He repaired and built ramparts, tightened frontier alerts, settled lawsuits, and encouraged agriculture and sericulture.

units.zh: 郡縣皆改節自勵，州內清肅，緣漢水陸千餘里，抄盜絕跡。
units.en: Commanderies and counties reformed their conduct and redoubled their efforts; the province grew orderly and calm, and along more than a thousand li of the Han by land and water, banditry disappeared entirely.
units.literal: Commanderies and counties all changed their conduct and encouraged themselves; within the province there was purity and solemnity; along the Han by land and water for more than a thousand li, banditry vanished without trace.

units.zh: 十一年，徵右衛將軍、領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In the eleventh year he was recalled as General of the Right Guard and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned as General of the Right Guard and placed in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 十二年，復爲使持節、督南北兗北徐青冀五州諸軍事、信威將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was again appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief over North and South Yan, North Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he again became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of the five provinces of North and South Yan, North Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 十三年，徵爲領軍將軍，直殿省，知十州損益事，月加祿五萬。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as General of the Palace Guard, attended at the Palace Hall Directorate, oversaw fiscal matters for ten provinces, and received a monthly salary increase of fifty thousand cash.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as General of the Palace Guard, attended at the Palace Hall Directorate, oversaw the profit-and-loss affairs of ten provinces, and received a monthly salary increase of fifty thousand.

units.zh: 景爲人雅有風力，長於辭令。
units.en: Jing carried himself with elegant force of character and was gifted in formal speech.
units.literal: Jing as a man had elegant bearing and strength of character, and excelled in rhetoric.

units.zh: 其在朝廷，爲衆所瞻仰。
units.en: At court everyone looked up to him.
units.literal: In court he was looked up to by the multitude.

units.zh: 於高祖屬雖爲從弟，而禮寄甚隆，軍國大事，皆與議決。
units.en: Although he was only Gaozu's cousin, the emperor treated him with exceptional honor and consulted him on every major military and state affair.
units.literal: Although in relation to Emperor Gaozu he was a cousin, the ceremonial regard placed on him was very lofty; on great affairs of army and state he was always consulted for deliberation and decision.

units.zh: 十五年，加侍中。
units.en: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Chief.

units.zh: 十七年，太尉、揚州刺史臨川王宏坐法免。
units.en: In the seventeenth year Prince Hong of Linchuan, Grand Commandant and Governor of Yangzhou, was dismissed for an offense.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year the Grand Commandant and Governor of Yangzhou, Prince of Linchuan Hong, was removed from office for an offense.

units.zh: 詔曰：「揚州應須緝理，宜得其人。
units.en: An edict said, "Yangzhou must be brought to order, and the right man is needed for the task.
units.literal: An edict said: "Yangzhou needs to be put in order and should have the right man.

units.zh: 侍中、領軍將軍吳平侯景才任此舉，可以安右將軍監揚州，並置佐史，侍中如故，卽宅爲府。」
units.en: Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Palace Guard, Marquis of Wuping Jing, has the talent for it. Let him serve as General of the Right for Pacification overseeing Yangzhou, with a full staff appointed, retain his post as Attendant-in-Chief, and make his residence the administrative seat."
units.literal: Attendant-in-Chief and General of the Palace Guard, Marquis of Wuping Jing, has the talent to undertake this; he may be made General of the Right for Pacification to oversee Yangzhou, with staff officers appointed, Attendant-in-Chief as before, and his residence made the administrative seat."

units.zh: 景越親居揚州，辭讓甚懇惻，至于涕泣，高祖不許。
units.en: Though only a cousin, Jing was now to govern Yangzhou. He declined with deep earnestness, even to tears, but Gaozu would not hear of it.
units.literal: Jing, though a more distant kinsman, was to govern Yangzhou; his refusal was very earnest, even to tears, but Emperor Gaozu would not allow it.

units.zh: 在州尤稱明斷，符教嚴整。
units.en: As governor he was especially famed for clarity and decisiveness; his orders and directives were strict and orderly.
units.literal: In the province he was especially famed for clarity and decisiveness; his orders and instructions were strict and orderly.

units.zh: 有田舍老姥嘗訴得符，還至縣，縣吏未卽發，姥語曰：「蕭監州符，火爄汝手，何敢留之！」
units.en: An old peasant woman once won a writ in a lawsuit; when she returned to the county seat the clerks did not issue it at once. She said, "Supervisor Xiao's writ will burn your hands off—how dare you hold it back!"
units.literal: An old peasant woman once obtained a writ after suing; returning to the county, the county clerks did not at once issue it; the old woman said: "Supervisor Xiao's writ will burn your hands—how dare you keep it!"

units.zh: 其爲人所畏敬如此。
units.en: Such was the awe in which he was held.
units.literal: Such was the fear and respect in which he was held.

units.zh: 十八年，累表陳解，高祖未之許。
units.en: In the eighteenth year he repeatedly petitioned to resign, but Gaozu would not allow it.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he repeatedly memorialized to resign; Emperor Gaozu did not grant it.

units.zh: 明年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢司霍三州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史。
units.en: The following year he was posted out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief over Ying, Si, and Huo, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.
units.literal: The next year he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the three provinces of Ying, Si, and Huo, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.

units.zh: 將發，高祖幸建興苑餞別，爲之流涕。
units.en: Before he departed, Gaozu came to the Jianxing Park to give him a farewell banquet and wept for him.
units.literal: As he was about to depart, Emperor Gaozu visited the Jianxing Park to give a farewell banquet and wept for him.

units.zh: 旣還宮，詔給鼓吹一部。
units.en: After returning to the palace, an edict granted him a full set of martial music.
units.literal: After returning to the palace, an edict granted him one set of martial music.

units.zh: 在州復有能名。
units.en: In Ying he again earned a reputation for capable administration.
units.literal: In the province he again had a reputation for ability.

units.zh: 齊安、竟陵郡接魏界，多盜賊，景移書告示，魏卽焚塢戍保境，不復侵略。
units.en: Qi'an and Jingling bordered Wei territory and were plagued by bandits. Jing sent formal notices across the border, and Wei promptly burned its stockades, held the frontier, and ceased its raids.
units.literal: Qi'an and Jingling commanderies bordered Wei territory and had many bandits; Jing sent letters of notice, and Wei at once burned the stockades and guarded the border, no longer invading.

units.zh: 普通四年，卒于州，時年四十七。
units.en: In the fourth year of Putong he died in office, at the age of forty-seven.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Putong he died in the province, aged forty-seven.

units.zh: 詔贈侍中、中撫軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: An edict posthumously appointed him Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Central Pacification Army, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Sash with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Central Pacification Army, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Sash with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 諡曰忠。
units.en: His posthumous title was Loyal.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal.

units.zh: 子勱嗣。
units.en: His son Mai succeeded to the title.
units.literal: His son Mai succeeded.

units.zh: 昌字子建，景第二弟也。
units.en: Chang, styled Zijian, was Jing's second younger brother.
units.literal: Chang, courtesy name Zijian, was Jing's second younger brother.

units.zh: 齊豫章末，爲晉安王左常侍。
units.en: At the end of the Qi dynasty he served as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jin'an.
units.literal: At the end of Qi in Yuzhang he served as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jin'an.

units.zh: 天監初，除中書侍郎，出爲豫章內史。
units.en: Early in Tianjian he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and posted out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and went out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.

units.zh: 五年，加寧朔將軍。
units.en: In the fifth year he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 六年，遷持節、督廣交越桂四州諸軍事、輔國將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
units.en: In the sixth year he was promoted to Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief over Guang, Jiao, Yue, and Gui, General Who Assists the State, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Governor of Guang.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of the four provinces of Guang, Jiao, Yue, and Gui, General Who Assists the State, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Army Commander, and Governor of Guang.

units.zh: 七年，進號征遠將軍。
units.en: In the seventh year his title was advanced to General Who Campaigns Afar.
units.literal: In the seventh year his title was advanced to General Who Campaigns Afar.

units.zh: 九年，分湘州置衡州，以昌爲持節、督廣州之綏建湘州之始安諸軍事、信武將軍、衡州刺史，坐免。
units.en: In the ninth year Xiang was divided to create Heng. Chang was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Suijian in Guang and Shi'an in Xiang, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and Governor of Heng, but was dismissed for an offense.
units.literal: In the ninth year Xiang province was divided to establish Heng province; Chang was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Suijian in Guang and Shi'an in Xiang, General of Trustworthy Martiality, and Governor of Heng, but was removed from office for an offense.

units.zh: 十三年，起爲散騎侍郎，尋以本官兼宗正卿。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and soon added the concurrent post of Director of the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and soon held that office concurrently as Director of the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 其年，出爲安右長史。
units.en: That same year he was posted out as Chief Clerk of the Right for Pacification.
units.literal: That year he went out as Chief Clerk of the Right for Pacification.

units.zh: 累遷太子中庶子、通直散騎常侍，又兼宗正卿。
units.en: He rose in succession to Palace Companion of the Crown Prince and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication, and again held the concurrent post of Director of the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Palace Companion of the Crown Prince and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication, and again served concurrently as Director of the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 昌爲人亦明悟，然性好酒，酒後多過。
units.en: Chang was also intelligent and perceptive, but he loved wine and often went to excess after drinking.
units.literal: Chang as a man was also clear-minded, but by nature he loved wine and after drinking often went to excess.

units.zh: 在州郡，每醉輒徑出入人家，或獨詣草野。
units.en: In the provinces he would wander drunk straight into people's houses or go alone into the countryside.
units.literal: In provinces and commanderies, whenever drunk he would go straight in and out of people's houses, or go alone to the wild grasslands.

units.zh: 其於刑戮，頗無期度。
units.en: In matters of punishment and execution he showed little restraint.
units.literal: As for punishments and executions, he had little regular measure.

units.zh: 醉時所殺，醒或求焉，亦無悔也。
units.en: Those he killed while drunk he might ask about when sober, yet he felt no remorse.
units.literal: Those killed while drunk, when sober he might seek them out, yet felt no regret.

units.zh: 屬爲有司所劾，入留京師，忽忽不樂，遂縱酒虛悸。
units.en: When the authorities impeached him he was detained in the capital, grew restless and despondent, and drowned himself in drink and anxious delusion.
units.literal: He happened to be impeached by the responsible offices, was detained in the capital, grew restless and unhappy, and then gave himself to drink and empty dread.

units.zh: 在石頭東齋，引刀自刺，左右救之，不殊。
units.en: In the eastern studio at Shitou he drew a knife and stabbed himself; his attendants saved him, and he did not die.
units.literal: In the eastern studio at Shitou he drew a knife and stabbed himself; attendants saved him, and he did not perish.

units.zh: 十七年，卒，時年三十九。
units.en: In the seventeenth year he died, at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he died, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 子伯言。
units.en: His son was Boyan.
units.literal: His son Boyan.

units.zh: 昂字子明，景第三弟也。
units.en: Ang, styled Ziming, was Jing's third younger brother.
units.literal: Ang, styled Ziming, was Jing's third younger brother.

units.zh: 天監初，累遷司徒右長史，出爲輕車將軍、監南兗州。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianjian, he rose through successive posts to right chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses, then went out as Light Chariot General and supervisor of South Yanzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, he rose through successive posts to right chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses, then went out as Light Chariot General and supervisor of South Yanzhou.

units.zh: 初，兄景再爲南兗，德惠在人，及昂來代，時人方之馮氏。
units.en: Earlier, his elder brother Jing had twice governed South Yanzhou, and his kindness and benefits remained among the people. When Ang came to replace him, people of the time compared them to the Feng clan.
units.literal: Earlier, his elder brother Jing had twice governed South Yanzhou, and his kindness and benefits remained among the people. When Ang came to replace him, people of the time compared them to the Feng clan.

units.zh: 徵爲琅邪、彭城二郡太守，軍號如先。
units.en: He was summoned to be administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, with his military title as before.
units.literal: He was summoned to be administrator of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, with his military title as before.

units.zh: 復以輕車將軍出爲廣州刺史。
units.en: He again went out as Light Chariot General and inspector of Guangzhou.
units.literal: He again went out as Light Chariot General and inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 普通二年，爲散騎常侍、信威將軍。
units.en: In Putong 2, he became Regular Attendant and General Who Inspires Trusting Awe.
units.literal: In Putong 2, he became Regular Attendant and General Who Inspires Trusting Awe.

units.zh: 四年，轉散騎侍郎、中領軍、太子中庶子，出爲吳興太守。
units.en: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Gentleman, Commander of the Central Army, and Household Attendant to the Crown Prince, then went out as administrator of Wuxing.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Gentleman, Commander of the Central Army, and Household Attendant to the Crown Prince, then went out as administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 大通二年，徵爲仁威將軍、衛尉卿，尋爲侍中，兼領軍將軍。
units.en: In Datong 2, he was summoned as General of Benevolent Awe and Commandant of the Guards, and soon became Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Commander of the Army.
units.literal: In Datong 2, he was summoned as General of Benevolent Awe and Commandant of the Guards, and soon became Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Commander of the Army.

units.zh: 中大通元年，爲領軍將軍。
units.en: In Zhongdatong 1, he became Commander of the Army.
units.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, he became Commander of the Army.

units.zh: 二年，封湘陰縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: In the second year, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyin county, with a fief of one thousand households.
units.literal: In the second year, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyin county, with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 出爲江州刺史。
units.en: He went out as inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: He went out as inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 大同元年，卒，時年五十三。
units.en: In Datong 1, he died, aged fifty-three.
units.literal: In Datong 1, he died, aged fifty-three.

units.zh: 諡曰恭。
units.en: His posthumous title was Gong.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.

units.zh: 昱字子真，景第四弟也。
units.en: Yu, styled Zizhen, was Jing's fourth younger brother.
units.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zizhen, was Jing's fourth younger brother.

units.zh: 天監初，除秘書郎，累遷太子舍人，洗馬，中書舍人，中書侍郎。
units.en: Early in Tianjian he was appointed Secretary and rose in succession to Attendant of the Crown Prince, Groom, Palace Secretary, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Secretary; he was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Crown Prince, Groom, Palace Secretary, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 每求自試，高祖以爲淮南、永嘉、襄陽郡，並不就。
units.en: He repeatedly asked for a chance to prove himself in office, but when Gaozu offered him Huainan, Yongjia, and Xiangyang commanderies, he declined them all.
units.literal: He repeatedly asked to prove himself; Emperor Gaozu offered him the commanderies of Huainan, Yongjia, and Xiangyang, but he accepted none.

units.zh: 志願邊州，高祖以其輕脫無威望，抑而不許。
units.en: He asked to serve on the frontier, but Gaozu, judging him frivolous and lacking authority, refused.
units.literal: He wished for a frontier province; Emperor Gaozu, because he was frivolous and without prestige, suppressed and did not grant it.

units.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Affairs.
units.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Affairs.

units.zh: 上表曰：「夏初陳啓，未垂采照，追懷慚懼，實戰胸心。
units.en: He submitted a memorial that read, "Early this summer I laid out my petition, yet Your Majesty has not yet looked upon it with favor. Thinking back on this fills me with shame and fear, and my heart trembles within my breast.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "At the beginning of summer I presented my petition, yet no favoring glance has fallen upon it; recalling this I feel shame and fear, and my heart truly trembles within my breast.

units.zh: 臣聞暑雨祁寒，小人猶怨；
units.en: I have heard that in summer rain and bitter winter cold even common people still complain;
units.literal: Your servant has heard that in summer rain and severe winter cold, even petty men still complain;

units.zh: 榮枯寵辱，誰能忘懷！
units.en: how much more when glory turns to decline, or favor to disgrace—who can put such things out of mind!
units.literal: glory and decline, favor and disgrace—who can forget them from the heart!

units.zh: 臣藉以往因，得預枝戚之重；
units.en: Through blessings from former lives I was allowed a place among the imperial kin;
units.literal: Your servant, relying on causes from the past, was able to share in the weight of the branch kin;

units.zh: 緣報旣雜，時逢坎鹆稟之運。
units.en: yet my karmic entanglements were already complex, and the age itself was one of hardship and reversal.
units.literal: because karmic retribution was already mixed, the times encountered a fate of hardship and setback.

units.zh: 昔在齊季，義師之始，臣乃幼弱，粗有識慮，東西阻絕，歸赴無由，雖未能負戈擐甲，實銜淚憤懣。
units.en: In the last years of Qi, when the righteous army first rose, I was still young, with only the beginnings of understanding. East and west were cut off, and I had no way to join the cause. Though I could not take up arms myself, I bore tears and burning indignation in my heart.
units.literal: Formerly in the closing years of Qi, at the beginning of the righteous army, your servant was still young and weak, with only rough understanding; east and west were cut off, and there was no way to return and join; though unable to bear spear and don armor, I truly held tears and smoldering indignation.

units.zh: 潛伏東境，備履艱危，首尾三年，亟移數處，雖復饑寒切身，亦不以凍餒爲苦。
units.en: I hid in the eastern borderlands and endured every hardship and danger. For three years I moved from place to place in haste. Though hunger and cold pressed upon me, I did not count freezing or starvation as suffering.
units.literal: Hiding in the eastern borderlands, I fully experienced hardship and peril; from beginning to end for three years I moved hurriedly to several places; though hunger and cold pressed on my person, I did not take freezing and starvation as suffering.

units.zh: 每涉驚疑，惶怖失魄，旣乖致命之節，空有項領之憂，希望開泰，冀蒙共樂；
units.en: Whenever danger struck I was terrified out of my wits. Having failed the duty of giving my life for the cause, I was left with nothing but the shame of an idle neck. I hoped for a new age of peace and longed to share in its joy.
units.literal: Whenever I encountered alarm and doubt I was terrified and lost my spirit; having failed the integrity of giving my life, I had only the worry of a neck left idle; I hoped for opening prosperity and wished to share joy together;

units.zh: 豈期二十餘年，功名無紀，畢此身骸，方填溝壑，丹誠素願，溘至長罷，俯自哀憐，能不傷歎！
units.en: Who could have foreseen that for more than twenty years I would win no record of merit, and that only when this body is spent will it fill some ditch? My earnest heart and lifelong hopes have suddenly reached their end. Looking down on myself in pity, how could I not grieve and sigh!
units.literal: Who could have expected that for more than twenty years achievement and fame were unrecorded, and that only when this body is finished will it fill a ditch and gully; red sincerity and plain wishes suddenly reach long cessation—bowing to pity myself, how could I not grieve and sigh!

units.zh: 夫自媒自衒，誠哉可鄙；
units.en: Self-promotion and self-display are truly contemptible;
units.literal: As for self-recommendation and self-display, truly they are contemptible;

units.zh: 自譽自伐，實在可羞。
units.en: self-praise and boasting are truly shameful.
units.literal: self-praise and self-boasting are truly shameful.

units.zh: 然量己揆分，自知者審，陳力就列，寧敢空言？
units.en: Yet having measured myself and appraised my place, I know myself clearly enough: to offer my strength and take up a post—how could that be mere empty talk?
units.literal: Yet measuring myself and appraising my portion, one who knows himself is careful; to display strength and take a place—how would I dare empty words?

units.zh: 是以常願一試，屢成干請。
units.en: That is why I have repeatedly asked for a chance to prove myself.
units.literal: For this reason I have constantly wished for one trial, and repeatedly made importunate requests.

units.zh: 夫上應玄象，實不易叨；
units.en: To match Heaven's hidden signs is no easy presumption;
units.literal: As for matching the dark signs above, it is truly not easy to presume upon;

units.zh: 錦不輕裁，誠難其制。
units.en: brocade is not cut lightly, and its making is truly difficult.
units.literal: brocade is not lightly cut—truly hard to fashion.

units.zh: 過去業鄣，所以致乖算測。
units.en: It is past karmic obstacles that have caused me to fall short of what was expected.
units.literal: Past karmic obstacles are the reason for causing departure from calculated expectation.

units.zh: 聖監旣謂臣愚短，不可試用，豈容久居顯禁，徒穢黃樞。
units.en: Since Your Majesty has judged me foolish and inadequate, unfit for trial in office, I cannot remain long in this exalted inner post, merely defiling the imperial pivot.
units.literal: Since the sage perception already holds your servant foolish and deficient and unfit for trial employment, I cannot long remain in the conspicuous forbidden precinct, vainly defiling the Yellow Pivot.

units.zh: 忝竊稍積，恐招物議，請解今職，乞摒退私門。
units.en: My unworthy tenure has gone on too long, and I fear public criticism. I beg to be relieved of my present office and sent back to private life.
units.literal: My unworthy usurpation has accumulated somewhat; I fear attracting public criticism; I beg to be released from my present office and ask to be cast back to a private gate.

units.zh: 伏願天照，特垂允許。
units.en: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty's gracious consent.
units.literal: Prostrate, I wish Heaven's illumination to grant permission especially.

units.zh: 臣雖叨榮兩宮，報效無地，方違省闥，伏深戀悚。」
units.en: Though I have enjoyed unearned honor in both palaces, I have had no way to repay it. As I leave the inner court, I prostrate myself in deep attachment and dread."
units.literal: Your servant, though enjoying unearned glory in both palaces, has no place to repay effectiveness; just now departing the inner gates, I prostrate deep attachment and dread."

units.zh: 高祖手詔答曰：「昱表如此。
units.en: Gaozu replied in his own hand: "Yu's memorial reads as follows.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu replied in his own hand: "Yu's memorial is as follows.

units.zh: 古者用人，必前明試，皆須績用旣立，乃可自退之高。
units.en: In antiquity, when appointing men to office, rulers always tested them first. Only after they had established a record of achievement could they withdraw to a lofty retirement.
units.literal: In antiquity when employing men, one must first clearly test them; all must have established achievement in office before they may retire to loftiness on their own.

units.zh: 昔漢光武兄子章、興二人，並有名宗室，就欲習吏事，不過章爲平陰令，興爲緱氏宰，政事有能，方遷郡守，非直政績見稱，卽是光武猶子。
units.en: In the past, Emperor Guangwu of Han's nephews Zhang and Xing were both eminent members of the imperial clan. When they wished to learn administration, Zhang was made only magistrate of Pingyin and Xing magistrate of Gou. Only when their governance showed ability were they promoted to commandery administrators. It was not merely that their achievements were praised—they were the emperor's own nephews.
units.literal: Formerly the Han Emperor Guangwu's brother's sons Zhang and Xing, both famed in the imperial clan, wished to learn administrative affairs; Zhang became no more than magistrate of Pingyin, Xing magistrate of Gou—only when their government affairs showed ability were they promoted to commandery administrators; it was not merely that their administrative achievements were praised, but they were Guangwu's nephews.

units.zh: 昱之才地，豈得比類焉！
units.en: How can Yu's talent and standing be compared with theirs!
units.literal: How can Yu's talent and standing be compared in kind!

units.zh: 往歲處以淮南郡，旣不肯行；
units.en: Last year he was offered Huainan commandery, yet refused to go;
units.literal: In past years he was placed in Huainan commandery, yet refused to go;

units.zh: 續用爲招遠將軍、鎮北長史、襄陽太守，又以邊外致辭；
units.en: then he was appointed General Who Summons the Distant, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, and again declined on the grounds that the post was on the frontier;
units.literal: he was next used as General Who Summons the Distant, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Xiangyang, and again declined on the grounds of the frontier;

units.zh: 改除招遠將軍、永嘉太守，復云內地非願；
units.en: he was then reassigned as General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Yongjia, and again said the interior was not what he wanted;
units.literal: he was changed and appointed General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Yongjia, and again said the interior was not his wish;

units.zh: 復問晉安、臨川，隨意所擇，亦復不行。
units.en: he was then offered Jin'an and Linchuan to choose as he pleased, and again he would not go.
units.literal: he was again asked about Jin'an and Linchuan, to choose as he wished, yet again would not go.

units.zh: 解巾臨郡，事不爲薄，數有致辭，意欲何在？
units.en: To take up office and govern a commandery is no slight honor. He has declined again and again—what does he want?
units.literal: To unbind the scarf and oversee a commandery is no slight matter; repeatedly he has declined—what is the intent?

units.zh: 且昱諸兄遞居連率，相繼推轂，未嘗缺歲。
units.en: Moreover Yu's elder brothers have held regional commands in succession, one after another, without a year's gap.
units.literal: Moreover Yu's elder brothers in succession have held regional command, one after another pushing the chariot wheel, never missing a year.

units.zh: 其同產兄景，今正居籓鎮。
units.en: His full brother Jing now holds a frontier fief and command.
units.literal: His full brother Jing now holds a frontier fief and command.

units.zh: 朕豈厚於景而薄於昱，正是朝序物議，次第若斯，於其一門，差自無愧。
units.en: Do I favor Jing and slight Yu? It is simply that court order and public opinion proceed in due sequence. For one family, the arrangement is not unreasonable.
units.literal: How would I favor Jing and slight Yu? It is precisely that court order and public opinion proceed in such sequence; for one family, it is rather without shame.

units.zh: 無論今日不得如此；
units.en: To say nothing of the present, when such a thing cannot be allowed;
units.literal: Not to speak of today when it cannot be so;

units.zh: 昱兄弟昔在布衣，以處成長，於何取立，豈得任情反道，背天違地。
units.en: the Yu brothers were raised from common life by circumstance. On what basis do they stand? They cannot follow whim against the Way or defy Heaven and earth.
units.literal: the Yu brothers formerly in plain cloth were raised by circumstance; on what basis do they stand? They cannot follow whim against the Way, turn their backs on Heaven, or violate Earth.

units.zh: 孰謂朝廷無有憲章，特是未欲致之于理。
units.en: Who says the court has no laws? I have simply not wished to bring him to judgment.
units.literal: Who says the court has no statutes and regulations? It is only that I have not wished to bring him to judgment.

units.zh: 旣表解職，可聽如啓。」
units.en: Since he has asked to resign, his request may be granted as stated."
units.literal: Since he has memorialized to resign from office, his request may be granted as stated."

units.zh: 坐免官。
units.en: He was dismissed from office.
units.literal: He was removed from office for the offense.

units.zh: 因此杜門絕朝覲，國家慶弔不復通。
units.en: Thereafter he shut his gate and ceased attending court; he no longer took part in state celebrations or mourning.
units.literal: Because of this he shut his gate and cut off court audiences; he no longer communicated in state celebrations or mourning.

units.zh: 普通五年，坐於宅內鑄錢，爲有司所奏，下廷尉，得免死，徙臨海郡。
units.en: In the fifth year of Putong he was impeached for casting coin in his home, sent to the Court of Justice, spared death, and banished to Linhai commandery.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, for casting coin within his residence he was impeached by the responsible offices, sent down to the Court of Justice, escaped death, and was banished to Linhai commandery.

units.zh: 行至上虞，有敕追還，且令受菩薩戒。
units.en: When he reached Shangyu, an edict recalled him and ordered him to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
units.literal: Traveling to Shangyu, an edict recalled him and ordered him to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

units.zh: 昱旣至，恂恂盡禮，改意蹈道，持戒又精潔，高祖甚嘉之，以爲招遠將軍、晉陵太守。
units.en: When Yu arrived, he was respectful in all ritual observance, turned his heart to the Way, and kept the precepts with pure devotion. Gaozu greatly praised him and appointed him General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Jinling.
units.literal: When Yu arrived, he was respectful and fulfilled all ritual; he changed his intent and followed the Way; his observance of precepts was also pure and scrupulous; Emperor Gaozu greatly praised him and made him General Who Summons the Distant and Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 下車勵名迹，除煩苛，明法憲，嚴於姦吏，優養百姓，旬日之間，郡中大化。
units.en: Upon taking office he set an example of integrity, removed oppressive regulations, clarified the laws, was stern with corrupt officials, and cared generously for the people. Within ten days the commandery was thoroughly transformed.
units.literal: Upon taking office he encouraged reputation and conduct, removed troublesome severity, clarified laws and statutes, was stern toward corrupt officials, and generously nurtured the people; within ten days the commandery was greatly transformed.

units.zh: 俄而暴疾卒，百姓行坐號哭，市里爲之喧沸，設祭奠於郡庭者四百餘人。
units.en: Soon he died suddenly of illness. The people wept wherever they walked or sat; the marketplaces rang with lamentation, and more than four hundred people set up offerings in the commandery court.
units.literal: Soon he died suddenly of illness; the people wept and wailed whether walking or sitting; the marketplaces were clamorous for it; more than four hundred set up offerings in the commandery court.

units.zh: 田舍有女人夏氏，年百餘歲，扶曾孫出郡，悲泣不自勝。
units.en: In the countryside a woman of the Xia clan, more than a hundred years old, supported her great-grandson to the commandery seat and wept until she could weep no more.
units.literal: In the countryside there was a woman of the Xia clan, more than a hundred years old, who supported her great-grandson to come out to the commandery seat, weeping in grief beyond control.

units.zh: 其惠化所感如此。
units.en: Such was the depth of feeling his benevolent rule inspired.
units.literal: Such was what his benevolent transformation moved.

units.zh: 百姓相率爲立廟建碑，以紀其德。
units.en: The people together built a temple and erected a stele to commemorate his virtue.
units.literal: The people in succession built a temple and erected a stele to record his virtue.

units.zh: 又詣京師求贈諡。
units.en: They also went to the capital to request a posthumous title for him.
units.literal: They also went to the capital to request a posthumous title.

units.zh: 詔贈湘州刺史。
units.en: An edict posthumously appointed him Governor of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Governor of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 諡曰恭。
units.en: His posthumous title was Respectful.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Respectful.

units.zh: 史臣曰：高祖光有天下，慶命傍流，枝戚屬㜕，咸被任遇。
units.en: The historian writes: When Gaozu came to possess the realm, fortune flowed to his kinsmen on every side, and collateral relatives of the imperial house were all given office and favor.
units.literal: The historian says: Emperor Gaozu possessed all under Heaven; felicitous mandate flowed to the sides; branch kin and collateral relatives were all given employment and favor.

units.zh: 蕭景之才辯識斷，益政佐時，蓋梁宗室令望者矣。
units.en: Xiao Jing's talent, judgment, and debate, and his service in strengthening the government of his time, made him the outstanding figure among the Liang imperial clan.
units.literal: Xiao Jing's talent in debate and judgment, benefiting government and assisting the age—he was perhaps the eminent hope of the Liang imperial clan.

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 臨川內史王觀，僧虔之孫，人身不惡，便可召爲長史，以代元沖。」
units.en: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, Sengqian's grandson, is not ill-favored—summon him as chief clerk for Yuanchong."
units.literal: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, grandson of Sengqian, is not ill-favored in person—call him in as chief clerk to replace Yuanchong."

units.zh: 年二十，遭王莽敗，世祖即位於冀州。
units.en: At twenty he lived through Wang Mang's fall and watched Liu Xiu raise the Han banner in Ji.
units.literal: At twenty he encountered Wang Mang's collapse, and the Founding Ancestor took the throne in Ji Province.

units.zh: 天監四年，大舉北伐，臨川王宏都督衆軍，以惔爲副。
units.en: In Tianjian year four the court launched a great northern campaign; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the armies with Tan as deputy.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, commanded the massed armies, with Tan as his deputy.

units.zh: 庚戌，以寧朔將軍蕭懿爲梁、南秦二州刺史，輔國長史申希祖爲交州刺史。
units.en: Day gengxu: Xiao Yi, pacifying-barbarians general, took Liang and South Qin; Shen Xizu, supporter-of-the-state chief clerk, took Jiaozhou.
units.literal: Day gengxu: Pacifying-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made inspector of Liang and South Qin; Supporter-of-the-State Chief Clerk Shen Xizu was made inspector of Jiaozhou.

units.zh: 尋除車騎將軍、江州刺史，副司徒建安王於赭圻，賜以諸葛亮筩袖鎧。
units.en: He was soon Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou, serving under the Minister of Works, Prince of Jian'an, at Zheqi, and was presented with Zhuge Liang's linked tube armor.
units.literal: Soon he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou, second to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Jian'an, at Zheqi, and was given Zhuge Liang's tube-and-sleeve armor.

units.zh: 舅吳平光侯蕭勱〔一〕，名重當時，特所鍾愛，嘗謂總曰：「爾操行殊異，神采英拔，後之知名，當出吾右。」
units.en: His maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping, [1] enjoyed a weighty reputation in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong, "Your conduct is wholly unlike that of others, and your spirit is striking and elevated; when you become famous hereafter, you will stand above me."
units.literal: His maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping, enjoyed a weighty reputation in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong: "Your conduct is wholly unlike that of others, and your spirit is striking and elevated; when you become famous hereafter, you will stand above me."

units.zh: 〔一〕 舅吳平光侯蕭勱 「勱」梁書蕭景傳、南史吳平侯景傳並作「勵」，南史江總傳又作「勱」。
units.en: On "his maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping": both the Book of Liang biography of Xiao Jing and the Southern History biography of Marquis Jing of Wuping write the final character of Mai's name as li; the Southern History biography of Jiang Zong again writes it as mai.
units.literal: [1] His maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping: both the Book of Liang biography of Xiao Jing and the Southern History biography of Marquis Jing of Wuping write the final character of Mai's name as li; the Southern History biography of Jiang Zong again writes it as mai.

units.zh: 按桂馥說文解字義證云「勱」字或作「勵」。
units.en: Gui Fu's Evidential Explanation of the Meanings of the Shuowen Jiezi says that the final character of Mai's name may also be written with the graph read "li".
units.literal: According to Gui Fu's Evidential Explanation of the Meanings of the Shuowen Jiezi, the final character of Mai's name may also be written with the graph read "li".

units.zh: 太祖文皇帝含光大之量，啓西伯之基。
units.en: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor held vast hidden brilliance and laid the foundation of the Western Earl.
units.literal: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor embraced a great measure of hidden light and opened the foundation of the Western Earl.

units.zh: 在襄陽拜表北伐，遣長史柳津、司馬董當門，壯武將軍杜懷寶、振遠將軍曹義宗等衆軍進討，剋平南陽、新野等郡，魏南荊州刺史李志據安昌城降，拓地千餘里。
units.en: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign and sent chief clerk Liu Jin, marshal Dong Dangmen, martial valor general Du Huaibao, far-shaking general Cao Yizong, and others with the armies; they took Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies, Wei's south Jingzhou inspector Li Zhi surrendered Anchang fortress, and territory expanded more than a thousand li.
units.literal: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign; he sent Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, Martial Valor General Du Huaibao, Far-Shaking General Cao Yizong, and others with the massed armies on expedition, conquering Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies; Wei's South Jingzhou Inspector Li Zhi, holding Anchang fortress, surrendered, and territory was extended more than a thousand li.

units.zh: 會賊唐㝢之作亂，稷率厲縣人，保全縣境。
units.en: When the bandit Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji led and encouraged the county people and preserved the county territory.
units.literal: When the bandit Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji led and encouraged the county people and preserved the county territory.
